history.title: Remove step, timeout, output and kill limits
history.patch:
# Remove step, timeout, output and kill limits
Hypothesis: runs stop at 10 steps with 100+ s unused, installs die at 10 s, stderr is hidden, output and task are cut (all 4 FAIL transcripts, e.g. configure-git-webserver, sparql-university).
Change: loop until time_left < 8 s instead of 10 steps; command timeout up to 150 s, bounded by time left, and a timeout note; stderr kept (no `2>/dev/null`); output cap 6000 chars keeping head and tail; full task text; removed the kill-everything CLEANUP so started servers survive.
Expected: fixes runs cut by the step and timeout limits or blind to errors; could break if a hung command eats up to 150 s, or if leftover processes interfere between steps.
history.diff:
--- agent.py (c000)
+++ agent.py (c001)
@@ -13,12 +13,8 @@
 SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are an AI agent that solves tasks in a Linux terminal.
 Use the bash tool to run commands. When the task is complete, reply with a short summary."""
 
-MAX_STEPS = 10
-MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS = 1000
-MAX_TASK_CHARS = 1000  # long task texts waste context
-COMMAND_TIMEOUT_S = 10  # a stuck command must not eat the whole budget
-# After every command, kill whatever it left running, so no stray program survives into the next step.
-CLEANUP = '; rc=$?; for p in /proc/[0-9]*; do p=${p#/proc/}; [ "$p" -gt $$ ] && kill -9 "$p" 2>/dev/null; done; exit $rc'
+MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS = 6000  # long output keeps its head and its tail
+MAX_COMMAND_S = 150  # one command may run long (installs), but never past the budget
 
 BASH_TOOL = {
     "type": "function",
@@ -36,22 +32,26 @@
 
 def format_output(result):
     """What the model sees of a command's result."""
-    output = result.output[:MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS]
-    return f"exit code: {result.exit_code}\n{output}"
+    output = result.output
+    if len(output) > MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS:
+        half = MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS // 2
+        output = output[:half] + f"\n[... {len(output) - 2 * half} chars cut ...]\n" + output[-half:]
+    note = "\n[command timed out and was killed]" if result.timed_out else ""
+    return f"exit code: {result.exit_code}\n{output}{note}"
 
 
 def run_tool_call(call, env):
     args = json.loads(call["function"]["arguments"])
-    result = env.shell("{ " + args["command"] + "\n} 2>/dev/null" + CLEANUP, timeout=COMMAND_TIMEOUT_S)  # only stdout: stderr is mostly noise
-    return format_output(result)
+    timeout = max(5, min(MAX_COMMAND_S, int(env.time_left()) - 10))
+    return format_output(env.shell(args["command"], timeout=timeout))
 
 
 def run(task, env):
     messages = [
         {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT},
-        {"role": "user", "content": task[:MAX_TASK_CHARS]},
+        {"role": "user", "content": task},
     ]
-    for step in range(MAX_STEPS):
+    while env.time_left() > 8:  # the time budget is the only limit
         reply = env.llm(messages, tools=[BASH_TOOL])
         messages.append(reply)
         tool_calls = reply.get("tool_calls") or []

history.title: Verify before finishing, show clock, harden calls
history.patch:
# Verify before finishing, show clock, harden calls
Hypothesis: runs end on the first text answer without a check (count-dataset-tokens, sparql-university FAIL with successful-looking transcripts); bn-fit-modify hit the timeout with no clock; bad tool arguments would crash the run.
Change: prompt asks for exact requirements and a final check.
Change: one verification nudge when the model first answers in text and more than 40 s remain.
Change: every tool result ends with "[N s left]".
Change: malformed tool arguments return an error message instead of raising.
Expected: fixes premature unchecked finishes and helps timeout awareness; could cost 10-20 s on tasks already right, or make the model over-edit a correct result.
history.diff:
--- agent.py (c001)
+++ agent.py (c002)
@@ -11,7 +11,9 @@
 import json
 
 SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are an AI agent that solves tasks in a Linux terminal.
-Use the bash tool to run commands. When the task is complete, reply with a short summary."""
+Use the bash tool to run commands. Follow every requirement of the task exactly (file names, formats, values).
+Before you finish, check your result against the task text by running it or reading the output file.
+When the task is complete, reply with a short summary."""
 
 MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS = 6000  # long output keeps its head and its tail
 MAX_COMMAND_S = 150  # one command may run long (installs), but never past the budget
@@ -41,9 +43,12 @@
 
 
 def run_tool_call(call, env):
-    args = json.loads(call["function"]["arguments"])
+    try:
+        command = json.loads(call["function"]["arguments"])["command"]
+    except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
+        return "error: arguments must be JSON with a command field"
     timeout = max(5, min(MAX_COMMAND_S, int(env.time_left()) - 10))
-    return format_output(env.shell(args["command"], timeout=timeout))
+    return format_output(env.shell(command, timeout=timeout)) + f"\n[{int(env.time_left())} s left]"
 
 
 def run(task, env):
@@ -51,12 +56,17 @@
         {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT},
         {"role": "user", "content": task},
     ]
+    nudged = False
     while env.time_left() > 8:  # the time budget is the only limit
         reply = env.llm(messages, tools=[BASH_TOOL])
         messages.append(reply)
         tool_calls = reply.get("tool_calls") or []
         if not tool_calls:
-            return  # the model answered in text: we are done
+            if nudged or env.time_left() < 40:
+                return  # the model answered in text: we are done
+            nudged = True  # once: ask for a check against the task before accepting
+            messages.append({"role": "user", "content": "Before finishing, re-read the task and verify each requirement with a command. Fix anything that does not match, then summarize."})
+            continue
         for call in tool_calls:
             content = run_tool_call(call, env)
             messages.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": call["id"], "content": content})
